title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: declarative agents ground answers in scanned PDFs from SharePoint
summary: The briefing's roadmap facts, licensing routes and control operations are supported. The Restricted Content Discovery path matches its cited page, although another Microsoft page uses a different setting label; that discrepancy merits a short note.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Scope; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Declarative agents can now ground answers in scanned PDFs referenced from SharePoint.
claims.quote: Any newly created Declarative Agents can now reliably ground answers in scanned PDFs and image-based documents referenced from SharePoint

claims.claim: The roadmap scopes the capability to newly created declarative agents.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes this enterprise content as previously hard to use in agent scenarios.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: The record does not say whether agents created earlier receive the capability, and Microsoft has not documented that distinction.
claims.quote: Searched: declarative agent SharePoint scanned PDF processing identity default enabled existing newly created agents; "declarative agents" "scanned PDFs". Read the roadmap, knowledge sources, Agent Builder, Toolkit and release notes; no older-agent coverage statement.

claims.claim: The roadmap does not describe how scanned content is read.
claims.quote: Any newly created Declarative Agents can now reliably ground answers in scanned PDFs and image-based documents referenced from SharePoint

claims.claim: The roadmap does not enumerate image-based file types beyond PDFs.
claims.quote: scanned PDFs and image-based documents referenced from SharePoint

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: The roadmap supplies no measured accuracy results.
claims.quote: Any newly created Declarative Agents can now reliably ground answers in scanned PDFs and image-based documents referenced from SharePoint, unlocking a major class of enterprise content that was previously hard to use in agent scenarios.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes the grounding as reliable.
claims.quote: can now reliably ground answers

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn has no documentation describing the specific scanned-PDF change in this roadmap item.
claims.quote: Searched: 550514 "scanned" "declarative"; "declarative agents" "scanned PDFs"; declarative agents SharePoint scanned PDF image based documents 550514 OCR disable setting default rollout older agents. Read knowledge sources, Agent Builder, Toolkit and release notes; no item-specific documentation.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated the feature's default state or what happens on arrival.
claims.quote: Searched: declarative agents SharePoint scanned PDF image based documents 550514 OCR disable setting default rollout older agents; declarative agent SharePoint scanned PDF processing identity default enabled existing newly created agents. Read roadmap and cited agent pages; no default stated.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: No admin, maker or automation setting specifically enabling or disabling scanned-PDF grounding is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: declarative agents scanned PDFs disable image understanding Microsoft Graph PowerShell setting; declarative agents SharePoint scanned PDF image based documents 550514 OCR disable setting default rollout older agents. Read Copilot settings, Agent Builder and knowledge sources; no such control.

claims.claim: The release notes contain an April 7, 2026 entry about embedded image understanding.
claims.quote:
## April 7, 2026
Updates released between March 24, 2026, April 7, 2026
Smarter answers with embedded image understanding

claims.claim: The embedded image entry is associated with roadmap ID 531758, a different item.
claims.quote:
Smarter answers with embedded image understanding
Roadmap ID: 531758

claims.claim: That separate entry describes declarative agents interpreting embedded images in .docx, .pptx and .pdf files.
claims.quote: What changed: Declarative Agents now analyze embedded images in supported file types (.docx, .pptx, .pdf).

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > All agents > agent > Block reaches the agent block action.
claims.quote: Select Agents > All agents. ... select an agent from the list of agents. ... immediately under the agent's name, select Block or Unblock.

claims.claim: POST /beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block blocks a Copilot package to prevent usage.
claims.quote:
Block a Copilot package to prevent its usage.
POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block

claims.claim: The Graph block call is a beta API.
claims.quote: APIs under the /beta version are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.claim: Access to the Graph Package Management API requires a Microsoft Agent 365 licence.
claims.quote: Access to the Package Management API requires a Microsoft Agent 365 license.

claims.claim: The Graph block method takes no request body.
claims.quote: Don't supply a request body for this method.

claims.claim: The admin centre Block action restricts the selected agent across the whole organisation.
claims.quote:
These actions apply to the selected agent.
Block and unblock | Restrict access to an agent across the organization, preventing any user from using it.

claims.claim: Blocking Agent Builder or Copilot Studio agents also affects availability and functionality in other host products.
claims.quote: It also affects availability and functionality in other host products, such as Microsoft Outlook, Microsoft Teams, or other Microsoft 365 applications.

claims.claim: Blocking agents created with SharePoint or Microsoft Foundry affects only their availability in Copilot Chat.
claims.quote: However, blocking an agent that you created by using SharePoint or Microsoft Foundry only impacts its availability in Microsoft Copilot Chat.

claims.claim: The agent-actions page does not specifically name agents built with Agents Toolkit.
claims.quote: Searched: Agents Toolkit and Toolkit in the complete agent-actions page. Its blocking passage names Agent Builder, Copilot Studio, SharePoint and Microsoft Foundry, not Toolkit.

claims.claim: The admin centre block-action page does not state the Graph reference's Microsoft Agent 365 licence requirement for that UI action.
claims.quote: Searched: license, licensing and Microsoft Agent 365 in the complete agent-actions page. Read its Block or unblock agents section; it does not attach the Package Management API licence requirement to the UI block action.

claims.claim: SharePoint admin center > Sites > Active sites > site > Settings > Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot reaches Restricted Content Discovery.
claims.quote: In the SharePoint admin center, expand Sites and select Active sites. Select the site you want to configure. Open the Settings tab, and then turn Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot on.
claims.fix: Keep the cited path. Add to the row note: 'Microsoft's Get ready for Microsoft 365 Copilot and agents with SharePoint Advanced Management page calls this setting Restrict content discovery.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/get-ready-copilot-sharepoint-advanced-management#step-3-prevent-accidental-oversharing, which says 'Under Restrict content discovery, select On.'

claims.claim: Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true enables Restricted Content Discovery for a site.
claims.quote: Enable Restricted Content Discovery for a site ... Use PowerShell ... Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery requires the organisation to be licensed for Copilot.
claims.quote: Ensure your organization has a Microsoft Copilot license.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery requires SharePoint Advanced Management to be available.
claims.quote: You can configure Restricted Content Discovery if your organization is licensed for Copilot and has SharePoint Advanced Management available.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery limits site content discovery in organisation-wide search and Microsoft Copilot responses.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery helps you limit discovery of content from specific SharePoint sites, including recently interacted files, in organization-wide search results and Microsoft Copilot responses

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery changes discoverability rather than existing access permissions.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery doesn't change existing permissions.

claims.claim: Users with existing permission can still directly access restricted content.
claims.quote: Users who already have access to content can continue to access that content directly.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery is a site-level setting for SharePoint sites.
claims.quote:
Restricted Content Discovery is a site-level setting.
You can only apply this feature to SharePoint sites.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery is not supported for OneDrive sites.
claims.quote: It's not supported for OneDrive sites.

claims.claim: The Restricted Content Discovery page does not explain how the setting applies to an agent pinned to a specific SharePoint item as knowledge.
claims.quote: Searched: Restricted Content Discovery declarative agents specific SharePoint URL knowledge pinned site. Read the complete Restricted Content Discovery page and Agent Builder knowledge page; site-context and open-document exceptions are stated, but pinned-agent retrieval is not specified.

claims.claim: By default only SharePoint administrators can manage Restricted Content Discovery.
claims.quote: By default, only SharePoint administrators can manage Restricted Content Discovery.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Cost and licensing; Scope
claims.claim: The knowledge sources page states that SharePoint and OneDrive knowledge require an active Microsoft 365 Copilot licence for the signed-in user.
claims.quote: SharePoint and OneDrive knowledge sources require the signed-in user to have an active Microsoft 365 Copilot license.

claims.claim: That page states that unlicensed requests fail with 'Sorry, I wasn’t able to respond'.
claims.quote: If the user doesn't have a license, requests fail with the message Sorry, I wasn’t able to respond.

claims.claim: The knowledge sources table marks SharePoint as requiring a licence or metered usage.
claims.quote:
License or metered usage required?
SharePoint | ✅ | ✅ | Yes

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Scope; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The prerequisites page also permits declarative-agent SharePoint data through usage-based billing without a full Copilot licence.
claims.quote:
Users can access Copilot Chat and agents without a full Copilot license.
Custom knowledge: SharePoint data | ❌ | ✅ | ✅

claims.claim: The usage-based route bills tenant-grounded agents in Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: Belong to tenants with pay-as-you-go billing enabled (consumed as Copilot Credits). ... Usage billing applies to agents grounded in tenant data

claims.claim: The usage-based route requires an Azure subscription.
claims.quote: An Azure subscription and billing policy setup in the Microsoft 365 admin center are required.

claims.claim: The usage-based route requires a billing policy set up in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: An Azure subscription and billing policy setup in the Microsoft 365 admin center are required.

claims.claim: For SharePoint-file knowledge, the billing policy must be connected to the SharePoint agents service.
claims.quote: For agents that use SharePoint files as knowledge sources, the billing policy must be connected to the SharePoint agents service

claims.claim: Users of that route must belong to the security group assigned to the billing policy.
claims.quote: users must be in the security group assigned to the billing policy.

claims.claim: The licensing model is mixed, reflecting Microsoft 365 Copilot licensing and an alternative usage-based billing route.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 with a Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license ... Usage-based billing (pay-as-you-go) ... Consumption is measured in Copilot Credits.

claims.quote: Searched: declarative agents scanned PDF grounding billing Copilot Credits price meter licensing. Read prerequisites and Billing rates and management; no separate scanned-PDF grounding meter is identified.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not published a licence specific to scanned-PDF grounding.
claims.quote: Searched: declarative agents scanned PDF grounding billing Copilot Credits price meter licensing. Read prerequisites and knowledge sources; they describe general agent entitlement, not a scanned-PDF-specific licence. The roadmap also names none.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not document a separate identity for scanned-content processing in this feature.
claims.quote: Searched: declarative agent SharePoint scanned PDF processing identity default enabled existing newly created agents. Read knowledge sources, Toolkit and Agent Builder; signed-in-user access is documented, but a distinct scanned-content-processing identity is not.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated a rollout mechanism specific to scanned-PDF grounding.
claims.quote: Searched: declarative agents SharePoint scanned PDF image based documents 550514 OCR disable setting default rollout older agents; 550514 "scanned" "declarative". Read roadmap and release notes; generic gradual deployment is described, not this item's rollout mechanism.

claims.claim: Agent Builder documentation says SharePoint cannot be used as a knowledge source while Restricted SharePoint Search is enabled.
claims.quote: If Restricted SharePoint Search is enabled, you can't use SharePoint as a knowledge source.
